title: The Architecture of the Cosmos: Judges, Thrones, and Builder-Works
summary: An extended treatment of how the cosmos is structured by divine operations: the Twelve Judges sent from the Father; the throne-structure of dominion at every degree; the three garments by which the Living Spirit clothes himself to build; the Call descending through the members of the soul to the First Man; the seven works of the Living Spirit; the five structures and other works built into the bodies of the bound archons; the four works of the Third Ambassador's revealing; the cosmic mirror-Wheel before the Gate of the King of Honor; and the three concentric Zones holding evil within good within divine governance.
organizing_principle: Survey of cosmic architecture proceeding through the divine builders — Father's judges, throne-bearers, Living Spirit, Great Builder, Third Ambassador — and the structures they impose: judges, thrones, garments, members, works, walls, wheels, zones.
